mentality.instructions: You manage my_team in a 90-minute football match. score.us is my_team's goals and score.them is the opponent's. A team that is behind late on needs goals and must take more risk; a team that is ahead late on should protect its lead; early on or when level, stay balanced. Which mentality should my_team play with now?

criteria.park_the_bus: Everyone defends deep to protect a lead late in the match, accepting almost no chances
criteria.defensive: Sit deeper and stay compact to hold on to a lead, creating fewer chances but conceding fewer
criteria.balanced: An even split between attack and defence, the normal approach when the match is level or there is plenty of time left
criteria.attacking: Push extra players forward to create more chances when a goal is needed, leaving more space behind
criteria.all_out_attack: Throw everyone forward to chase a goal when losing near the end, leaving the defence badly exposed

press_high.instructions: Should my_team press high from now on? Pressing wins the ball back sooner but tires players faster, which hurts most when fitness is already low.

criteria.true: Press high to win the ball back quickly, at the cost of tiring faster

substitution.instructions: my_team has subs_left substitutions left for the whole match. Should my_team make a substitution now? Most of the time the right answer is none; save substitutions for when tiredness or the score calls for one.

criteria.none: Make no change and keep the substitutions for later
criteria.fresh_legs: Replace tired players with fresh ones when fitness has dropped low, restoring energy
criteria.extra_striker: Bring on an extra striker when a goal is needed late on, adding attack but weakening the defence
criteria.extra_defender: Bring on an extra defender to protect a lead late on, adding defence but blunting the attack

concern.instructions: How worried should the manager of my_team be about the final result right now?
criteria: Slightly uneasy: things are mostly going to plan
Uneasy: the result could go either way
Worried: the result is slipping away
Very worried: likely to lose unless something changes
